name: Kuni Ryōsei
concept: Her fingernails are worn flat on one side from years of scraping dried components off cataloging surfaces, and she does not file them even.

answers.stand_out: During her final examination at the dōjō, she sat across from her instructor in absolute silence for two hours, watching him perform a warding ritual, and when he asked her what she had learned, she described not the words or gestures but the precise moment when his concentration shifted — and was right.

answers.social_giri: Ryōsei serves Kuni Isei, who has placed her as yoriki under the Emerald Magistrate Kitsuki Nagiko; she catalogs the ritual components confiscated from mahō-tsukai cells, cross-referencing their uses against Kuni doctrine so that none are ever used twice.

answers.social_ninjo: She wants to build a ward that holds against mahō itself rather than merely containing it, and she has already sketched the framework using principles the Kuni would call heresy if they knew how far she had taken them.

answers.clan_relations: She recites the Kuni's purification rites word-perfect in formal settings and improvises variations in the field without asking permission, trusting her reading of the moment more than the prescribed text.

answers.success: She identified the mahō components in Magistrate Nagiko's first confiscation by their absence—the ones that should have been there, cross-referenced against three separate Kuni catalogs, and proved the cell had sold their most potent materials to an outsider before the raids began.

answers.difficulty: She cannot walk into a room where mahō components have been cataloged without her hands moving toward the work, and she has learned to disguise this as professional thoroughness.

answers.calms: She sits in the confiscation archive after the magistrate has left, a cup of last year's Kuni sake warming in her hands, reading the notes on components she has already memorized—not for the work, but because the repetition settles the wanting down to a hum she can live with.

answers.worries: She sketched a ward that should hold against mahō itself, showed it to Nagiko because protocol demanded it, and watched his face close the moment he understood what she had actually built.

answers.most_learn: Katsuhito — Katsuhito, a rōnin who had served three Kuni, taught Ryōsei to catalog a confiscation before touching any of it, and to touch none of it alone.

answers.first_sight: Her fingernails are worn flat on one side from years of scraping dried components off cataloging surfaces, and she does not file them even.
answers.accoutrement: Leather glove. Right hand, palm patched with canvas.

answers.stress: She stops speaking mid-sentence and begins examining whatever is nearest to her with absolute attention—the grain of wood, the weave of fabric, the way light falls across a surface—until someone directly addresses her by name.

answers.relations: Iuchi Okura (Unicorn) — Iuchi Okura taught her a Unicorn binding technique for containing volatile components, and now Ryōsei uses it on every catalog she prepares, which means every confiscation she handles carries a foreign mark that could get her examined if anyone looked closely enough.

answers.parents_pov: Her mother finds her impossible to shop for because she will spend twenty minutes examining the weave of a bolt of silk or the grain of a tea bowl and then say nothing about whether she wants it.

answers.death: She dies in the confiscation archive after hours, alone with a ward design that finally holds, before she can decide whether to burn it or show it to Nagiko.
